rationale: Requires successful identity verification of the analyst before access, which is authentication.
Restricts who may modify tax and pay-grade tables to a payroll administrator, a modification-control rule.
Verifies user identity via a master secret to unlock the credentials store, which is authentication.
Checks login name and secret against the registered account before access, i.e. credential authentication.
A keyed MAC makes unauthorised edits to log content detectable, protecting data integrity.
Validates the coherence and correctness of reservation data, with no attack explicitly mentioned.
Tamper-detection marking must stay verifiable (integrity) even under deliberate attempts to strip it (resisting intentional attack).
Compares a cryptographic digest and refuses installation on mismatch, detecting altered packages.
Requires verified credential check of clinician identity and denies entry otherwise.
Timestamps or counters let the receiver discard repeated updates, which is replay protection.
Validates format and checksum of account number input and rejects malformed entries, an accuracy check.
Identifies staff at sign-in by checking a secret code against the registered one, i.e. authentication.
Verifies format and precision of account numbers and amounts before recording, validating data accuracy.
A decoy endpoint that raises alerts and blocks the source detects and blocks intrusions.
Salary files must be sent only over an encrypted protocol, protecting them from disclosure.
Overwriting memory that held balances prevents residual data disclosure to other processes.
Encrypts stored results so only key holders can read them.
A checksum makes any alteration of the object file detectable.
The balance must be unreadable (confidentiality) and unalterable (integrity) by external devices outside defined commands.
Limits an authenticated session per account and rejects concurrent sign-in with the same credentials, touching credential authentication; whether it aims at resisting credential abuse is not stated.
Lets the owner verify that stored snapshots have not been changed since capture.
Stateful tracking that discards packets outside legitimate exchanges blocks malicious network traffic.
A verification code over transaction data detects modification in transit and the payment is declined, protecting integrity.
Only the administrator may undo configuration changes, restricting who can modify device configuration.
Protects personal data from unconsented disclosure (privacy) and requires detecting and blocking exfiltration via compromised accounts.
Suppresses messages that would expose account holder details contrary to privacy rules.
Terminating idle sessions explicitly to prevent a hijacker from taking over the connection limits attacker abuse.
Compares recomputed integrity codes to detect corrupted data and restores affected records.
Digital signature on firmware packages makes post-signing modification detectable; origin verification is not stated.
Verifying the signature against the account holder's registered key confirms the instruction's origin and that it was not altered.
A keyed MAC on exchanged salary files is used so that any modification is detected.
